program_name: Graduation of the Ultra Poor Pilot
intervention_description: A graduation approach targeting ultra-poor households with asset transfers, coaching, skills training, and consumption support

intervention_start.literal_text: Program activities began in October 2018 when individual and group life-skills coaching was launched

intervention_end.literal_text: Implementation of the graduation pilot was completed in Negros Occidental in September 2020

final_followup.literal_text: Between September and December 2021, IPA conducted an endline survey

graduation_components_rationale.assets: One-time asset transfer worth 15,000-20,000 pesos per recipient
graduation_components_rationale.skills_training: Business planning, organization, and accounting training
graduation_components_rationale.savings: Facilitated savings and microfinance institution access
graduation_components_rationale.coaching: Individual and group life skills coaching sessions
graduation_components_rationale.social_empowerment: Group membership and community mobilization activities

outcomes.outcome_description: Monthly consumption per capita in Philippine pesos
outcomes.literal_text: Monthly consumption per capita is between 311 to 342 pesos greater than the average among control-group households

outcome_timing_anchor.literal_text: Endline survey conducted between September and December 2021

outcomes.outcome_description: Composite food security index in standard deviations
outcomes.literal_text: Food security increased by 0.20 (T1) to 0.28 (T3) standard deviations across treatment arms

outcome_timing_anchor.literal_text: Endline survey conducted between September and December 2021

outcomes.outcome_description: Value of productive assets in Philippine pesos
outcomes.literal_text: Treatment households owning 1,954 to 4,484 pesos worth more productive assets than control households

outcome_timing_anchor.literal_text: Endline survey conducted between September and December 2021

outcomes.outcome_description: Percentage point increase in business ownership
outcomes.literal_text: T3 had a 9 percentage point increase in business ownership compared to 4 percentage points in T2 (p=0.02)

outcome_timing_anchor.literal_text: Endline survey conducted between September and December 2021

outcomes.outcome_description: Percentage point increase in savings and amount in Philippine pesos
outcomes.literal_text: Treatment households were 6-15 percentage points more likely to have savings, with 224-443 pesos more in savings

outcome_timing_anchor.literal_text: Endline survey conducted between September and December 2021

notes: Graduation pilot in Philippines testing individual vs group livelihoods and coaching models
